title: Personal Finance Lessons from Indian Scriptures: Earn, Share, Save
intro: Old stories often hide practical money advice. Here are some lessons from Indian scriptures that still hold up.

p: In a Bhavishya Purana story, a man named Kalavidu says he divides his daily earnings into five parts: for charity and religious duties, for sacrifices, for himself, for his wife and for food. The idea is simple: give income a purpose before it disappears.

The Puranas praise giving, but also say that a gift to a person with no need or respect for it is wasted, like water poured in a raw clay pot. Giving with care and knowledge is a form of wise spending.
The Puranas also praise planting trees and digging ponds, benefits that last for generations. In money terms, it is the habit of building something that outlives you.
Many texts warn against borrowing beyond one's means. A simple rule is to keep monthly loan payments well below your income.
Try dividing a salary into: needs, savings and investments, giving, and personal enjoyment. The exact split is yours, but having a plan matters.

faq.q: Do the scriptures talk about money?
faq.a: Yes. They treat artha, wealth, as one of the four goals of life, when earned fairly and used well.
No. It is a reflection to inspire good habits.
